title: Tesserae transport manifest
description: Shape of transport.json. Declares one delivery channel by which devices receive frames + post status: MQTT (push, subscribed to a broker), REST (pull, polled over HTTP), or whatever future shapes land. Manifests are metadata-only: the actual transport implementation lives in app/transport.py (MQTT) or app/rest_api.py (REST). The transport_loader discovers manifests at startup so the Settings UI can show which transports are active without each transport having to register itself in code.

tesserae_compat.description: Major version range this transport works against (e.g. '1.x'). The loader rejects mismatches.

id.description: Unique transport id, matches the folder name under transports/. Used as Device.transport's value when assigning a device to this transport.

kind.description: Whether the transport pushes frames to devices (e.g. MQTT publish) or serves them on pull (e.g. HTTP GET). Informational; the push pipeline branches on this to know whether transport.publish gets called per render.

broker_required.description: True when the transport needs a broker / external service (MQTT). False for self-contained transports (REST, served by Tesserae itself). Used by the Settings UI to hint at setup requirements.

capabilities.description: Per-feature capability map. Each entry is a boolean. Recognised keys: frame_delivery, device_status, device_config, discovery, retain_semantics, push_to_device.

default_for_new_devices.description: Whether the onboarding wizard / Pair card defaults to this transport when adding new devices. Only one transport should declare this true; if multiple do, the loader picks the first alphabetically.
